Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 12205 of 2022
Applicant :- Kaushlandra And Another
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajesh Kumar Yadav

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. C-04 of 2009, under sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station- Kotwali,
District- Mainpuri.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that they are innocent and have been falsely implicated in this case.

In this case, after investigation, charge sheet was submitted by the police before the learned court in the year 2009 which was challenged before this Court in which direction was made vide order dated 18.3.2011 in an application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No. 8759 of 2011 to file discharge application before the learned court and till disposal of the application, no coercive steps Kaushlandra And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153728410/
1 were to be taken.

entities.text: Kaushlandra And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In pursuance of the order of this Court, discharge was filed before the learned court but it remained pending and again he filed discharge application before the learned court which was disposed of.
Later on, he filed anticipatory bail application before the learned court but it was rejected.

Further submitted that applicant no. 2 Bhupendra is suffering from cancer and getting treatment in AIMS and applicant no. 1 is his brother and has to look after him in the hospital that was the reason they could not appear before the learned court.

It is also submitted that co-accused Mahraj Singh and Ajendra Singh have already been granted anticipatory bail by coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.9890 of 2022 vide order dated 20.10.2022.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.9890 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The case of these applicants stands on similar footing to that of co-accused persons.
They are ready to face the trial, therefore, requested for anticipatory bail during pendency of trial.
Learned AGA has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

On considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A. and the perusal of record and the fact that co-accused persons have already been granted anticipatory bail and the case of the present applicants is on similar footing, there appears ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of applicants during pendency of trial.

Order Date :- 23.3.2023 A. Singh  Kaushlandra And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153728410/
2
